issues.body:
Parent: [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018) (Atlas ingestion program). Statements S39–S40 of the 2026-11-04 brief.

## Mandate (Drew, in substance)

Alongside the smaller per-topic designs, produce **one larger design that expands the depth and scope of Atlas wherever the research takes it, thinking ahead to v2, v3, and v4** — not a restatement of the brief, but the brief pushed further: what does a personal corpus become when ingestion is automatic, provenance is complete, versions are kept, and every search can be judged by its user?

## Starting threads (research is expected to find more)

- **Feedback-trained retrieval**: thumbs/essay feedback + per-stage score traces (sibling design under [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018)) as training signal — per-user ranking adaptation, query-pattern evolution, and honest evaluation harnesses that distinguish "the corpus lacks it" from "the ranker buried it".
- **Provenance-complete resolution**: with [#3125](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3125)'s occurrence registry + version lineage, any chunk resolves to every place it ever lived, at every version — citation-grade answers ("this claim came from file X at commit Y, lines 17–241, also present in Z").
- **Cross-source lineage graph**: files, embeds, sessions, issues, notes as one graph (ties to the ID graph and the zettel graph designs; writer-set authority per [#5545](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5545)).
- **Self-curating corpus**: retention driven by measured usefulness (retrieval survival + feedback), not just age — the corpus proposes its own cold-storage and deletion candidates for human approval.
- **Classification-aware retrieval**: tier boundaries enforced inside ranking/expansion (a secret-tier chunk never hydrates an internal-tier context), building on the classification manifest line ([#5410](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5410)).
- **Cost-aware tiering**: hot/warm/cold placement continuously rebalanced against the plan ceiling (Turso/D1/rustfs per the 2026-11-04 storage ruling).
- **Agent-facing corpus**: Atlas as the memory substrate for agents — session/chat/report ingestion (operations design, sibling under [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018)) makes every agent's past work searchable by every future agent, with provenance spans as the trust mechanism.

## Method

Survey before designing: personal-knowledge/search systems (Mem, Rewind-style capture, Khoj, Quivr, personal RAG stacks), provenance systems (W3C PROV, git-like content addressing, datalake lineage), and feedback-loop retrieval research. Label dead ends as dead ends. Each v2/v3/v4 claim must name its dependency on the v1 pieces (delta ingestion, versioning, traces) so the horizon stays buildable, not aspirational.

## Done looks like

A design document in code (`doc/`) laying out the v2/v3/v4 arc with per-stage entry criteria, plus a follow-on issue list for anything the research shows is independently buildable sooner. Breadth is the deliverable; premature implementation commitments are explicitly out of scope.

issues.body:
## Program (Drew, 2026-11-04)

A long-term plan for **semi-automating updates to Atlas ingestion**: what gets ingested, how content is versioned, a standard provenance model, delta-only updates, retrieval statistics + result feedback, classification safety, and disk/IO + plan-spend discipline. Statement inventory (S1–S40, auditable, with per-statement dispositions): `~/workspace/scratch/atlas-ingestion-brief-2026-11-04/statement-inventory.md` in the sandbox workspace; this issue is the canonical tracker — children are linked in a comment below and closed into this issue as they complete.

## Where Atlas stands (2026-11-04, verified)

- Shard restoration complete: 31 TursoDB shards; **internal = 28 shards / 107,001 chunks; secret = exactly 1 shard / 638 chunks** (secret material only in the 2 secret DBs). Production monolith stays libSQL for now; TursoDB for all NEW databases. Cold tiers → rustfs (2026-11-04 storage ruling). Current spend anchor: **Turso scaler $24.92/mo yearly — the plan is the ceiling** (see also [#5468](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5468), mirror storage pressure).
- Search: fan-out over shards [#5755](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5755); query front-end [#5773](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5773); full parameter surface with per-run vector logging [#5774](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5774); Jaccard rescore + ingest dedup ≥0.9 recorded edge [#5733](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5733); staging tier with merge-on-close promotion [#5669](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5669).
- Provenance registry already designed: [#3125](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3125) (chunk_occurrences, content-addressed extracts, `repo@commit:path` pinning). This program **extends** #3125 (source-system marks, version lineage) rather than replacing it.
- Scripts migration into code + fleet binary: [#5670](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5670). Untracked Atlas material enumeration: [#5981](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5981) — ingestion source enumeration overlaps it.

## Topic map (children filed under this tracker)

1. **Ingestion operations design** — semi-automated updates; automatic source set (reboots/boot records, session logs, chat logs, statistics, reports); usefulness filter; disk + I/O monitoring; plan-spend ceiling.
2. **Classification revalidation (task)** — verify nothing sensitive sits at the wrong tier.
3. **Agent notes placement design** — zettel vs repo vs publishing directly into the ID graph (ties to [#5545](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5545), [#5686](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5686)).
4. **GitHub corpus extraction (task)** — ALL issue/PR comments from ALL our repos; external repos we interact with or rely on (external half gated, see 5).
5. **External-content licensing gate (research)** — may we copy external GitHub comments/discussions into Atlas at all? In the [#5977](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5977)/[#5986](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5986) family. **Must be answered before external-repo ingestion is built; design may proceed.**
6. **First-pass corpus (task)** — all code repos, all findable docs, dezren39/cairn.
7. **Content versioning + retention design** — new versions, rename lineage, newest-resolution ("take the max"), cold rollout, deletion triggers (date / superseding increments / never accessed).
8. **Retrieval statistics + feedback + query trace design** — top-K shard survival, top-1/2/3/5 after merge+rescore, thumbs up/down minimum, optional comments/essays, result↔query trace (per-stage scores, shard, exact embed state, metadata).
9. **Provenance standard** — extensions filed as a comment on [#3125](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3125): one standard for when/where; marks of the form `repo@hash:path` AND source-system marks (e.g. `opencode-db @ amd @ <date>`); segment search to associate unlineaged files; unassociated/duplicate as a logged state.
10. **Existing-embed provenance audit (task)** — scan all current embeds for correct path/provenance details.
11. **Delta-only ingestion + offset embeds design** — the 21 GB rule (20.5 GB already present → only new files + edits land; no mass retagging); span-anchored embeds (content at file offsets 17–241) with search-time joins that never double merged lines.
12. **Expansive v2–v4 design** — the larger design that pushes depth/scope beyond this brief wherever research leads.

## Horizons

- **v1** — first-pass corpus (own repos incl. GitHub comments, docs, cairn) + delta ingestion + provenance marking standard + embed audit + classification revalidation run.
- **v2** — file versioning/retention live (cold rollout + deletion policy) + retrieval statistics (shard survival, top-1/2/3/5).
- **v3** — feedback loop live (thumbs/comments/traces) feeding retention + ranking evolution; classification revalidation recurring/automated; offset-embed joins in production search.
- **v4** — expansive: feedback-trained ranking, provenance-complete resolution, cross-source lineage graph, ID-graph-native corpus objects, classification-aware retrieval.

## Gates

- External-repo comment ingestion is **build-gated** on topic 5's answer (Drew's sequencing: licensing figured out before the external build, after the design is somewhat done). Our own repos are not gated.
- Nothing in this program raises spend past the current plan without Drew's explicit call (S3).

issues.body:
## Direction (Drew, 2026-10-31)

Atlas moves from a single canonical DB + one Turso publish to provenance-first, scalable infrastructure. Design doc: hatch-personal `workspace/turso-atlas/docs/atlas-provenance-and-scale-design-2026-10-31.md`.

Rules:
1. Keep ALL data — nothing stripped from atlas.db or publishes to save space; only byte-identical dupes are cleaned, backups kept.
2. Backups AND plain extracts for every corpus.
3. Every chunk records EVERY place it was found: `chunk_occurrences` (chunk → array of source locators with spans, observed_at). Today dedup silently drops occurrences (~127K at first ingest); 6,344 canonical sessions own zero chunks for exactly this reason and their occurrences are unrecorded.
4. Every import is interned content-addressed (laptop extracts CAS / R2, registry maps CA hash → normal paths) or pinned as `repo@commit:path`. Registry also holds line numbers / dates / spans for extracts.
5. Retrieval: vector/FTS search across multiple Turso shard DBs (collection × month) returns IDs; a catalog/registry resolves an ID to a file, a chunk, or a start–end section — including a member of a tar in R2 (sidecar index, range fetch) or a local file.

Verified state feeding this (2026-10-31): canonical 18,325 sessions / 122,124 messages / 107,639 chunks; local-only = 6,941 chunks of personal-client TEXT held back from Turso by policy (not missing embeddings); Turso atlas 1.0 GB / 100,698 chunks; laptop ~/atlas 12 GB contains NO consequential byte-identical duplicates (hash-verified) — it is distinct versions/working sets, so no cleanup windfall exists.

## Phases
1. Add `chunk_occurrences` + `cas_registry` to canonical atlas.db; ingest writes occurrences from now on (no re-embed, no republish).
2. Laptop extracts dir + CAS; atlas-backup covers it; backfill extracts for sources still on disk.
3. Occurrence backfill from CAS extracts; document the local-only publish predicate in the publish script.
4. Catalog DB + shard layout at next publish growth (or full message-archive ingest); resolution as MCP tools (search → ids → resolve → fetch span).

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=muse state=filed source=main-chat-2026-10-31 -->

## Acceptance criteria

- A `chunk_occurrences` provenance registry exists: every chunk records every source locator it was found at (with spans and observed_at), including occurrences previously dropped by dedup.
- Backups AND plain extracts exist for every corpus; imports are interned content-addressed (CAS hash → path registry) or pinned as `repo@commit:path`, with line numbers / dates / spans recorded for extracts.
- Retrieval works across multiple Turso shard DBs (collection × month): vector/FTS search returns IDs and the catalog/registry resolves an ID to a file, chunk, or start–end section (including a tar member in R2 via sidecar index + range fetch, or a local file).
- No data is stripped to save space; only byte-identical duplicates are cleaned, with backups kept.

issues.body:
Follow-on to epic #5350 (Atlas binary + service), to be scheduled AFTER step 6 (cutover). Design only — no implementation in this issue.

## Where things stand
atlas-core's filter surface is split: the *vocabulary* is data-driven (filters match the labels the classification pass wrote onto chunks — kinds, topics, projects, clients — so new labels are filterable immediately), but the *dimensions and semantics* are hand-coded in four places (atlas-core `filters` module + SQL builders, the CLI flag surface, atlas-proto request types, serve-mode validation). Adding a new classification dimension today (e.g. a source-app label) requires a code change in each place. Match semantics are likewise code: exact match today, with LIKE-pattern matching tracked separately in #5375.

## Proposal (for a design note)
A classification manifest — carried with the corpus publish metadata — declares the filterable dimensions and their match semantics (exact / pattern / range), and atlas-core builds its filter surface from that manifest, with the CLI and service inheriting the same surface through atlas-proto. A reclassification pass could then change what searches can slice by without a binary release.

## Hard constraint
The sensitivity ladder and ceiling semantics stay CODE-defined, never data-defined. The ceiling is a safety property enforced inside branch SQL (filter-before-rank); a mislabeled or corrupted row must never be able to redefine its own visibility. Only dimension declarations and match semantics for non-sensitivity fields are manifest material.

## Open questions for the design
- Manifest home: publish-file metadata vs a DB table vs both (local mode vs Turso mode must agree).
- Versioning + failure mode: manifest unreadable/mismatched → fall back to the built-in surface, loudly, never silently widen.
- Interaction with #5375's pattern filters (land exact+pattern semantics once, in the manifest, rather than twice).
- Dedupe-key impact: serve-mode Computations key on the effective filter tuple — a manifest change must version into the key.

Acceptance for this issue: a design note under doc/ following the epic's design-note pattern, with a go/no-go recommendation.
